_note: Curated map: corpus-file miss record -> guide_en.md Part I sections. Verified by keyword probe bounded to lines 116-1510 (see WIP-GUIDE-HTML build log). Counts come from EXAM-LOG.md Professor's Notes plus the exact per-question data for Exams 12 and 13.

2.3.label: Missed twice in fourteen hours
2.3.text: Exam 12 Q33 and Exam 13 Q46 both asked which setting guarantees a tool call. You answered auto plus a prompt instruction both times, with the full explanation read in between. The two stems share only 0.118 similarity, so this is not a repeated question — it is a held preference. The setting outranks the instruction: auto permits text, full stop.

5.3.label: Three wrong picks across two papers
5.3.text: Exam 12 Q1 (answer was /memory), Exam 12 Q56 (answer was .claude/commands/), Exam 13 Q41 (answer was to delete prose from CLAUDE.md). Three different right answers, one recurring instinct. Rules answer “which files”. If the question is not about which files, it is not rules.

5.1.label: The §3.1 family has cost you four papers
5.1.text: Concatenation, not override. Every discovered file contributes, root down to the working directory. If two of them conflict, both are in context and you fix the files — nothing silently wins.

5.8.label: Missed on Exam 12 Q1
5.8.text: When a rule is followed on one machine and not another, the first move is diagnostic, not structural. Check which memory files actually loaded before you move anything anywhere.

5.4.label: Missed on Exam 12 Q56
5.4.text: Version-controlled and ships with the clone is the whole point of the project path. ~/.claude/commands/ reaches nobody else on the team.

13.1.label: Missed on Exams 4 and 5
13.1.text: Glob matches file paths. Grep searches file contents. “Find everywhere this symbol is used” is a content question every single time.

9.1.label: Both directions have cost you a paper
9.1.text: Exam 11 escalated an ambiguity that one question would have resolved. Escalate on structural signals — policy gap, an explicit request for a human, repeated failure. Not on how upset someone sounds, and not on a model's own confidence score.

7.5.label: Missed on Exam 12 Q57
7.5.text: You chose a synchronous fallback. Batch has no latency SLA, so the plan is arithmetic, not a safety net: submission deadline = downstream deadline minus 24 hours.

1.2.label: Missed on Exam 12 Q18
1.2.text: Tool results re-enter as structured tool_result blocks matched to their tool_use by id. Narrating what the tool returned in prose is not the protocol, so the call stays unanswered.

2.2.label: Missed on Exam 13 Q19
2.2.text: When a tool's behaviour surprises the agent — truncation limits, what it cannot reach — the fix is to state it in the description. The description is the model's only view of scope.

6.1.label: Missed on Exam 12 Q6
6.1.text: Prose instructions already failed. Adding a post-processing repair stage leaves generation exactly as unreliable as it was; examples of the exact shape are the documented fix.

3.3.label: Missed on Exam 12 Q17
3.3.text: Subagents never see the coordinator's history. When one reports it has nothing to work with, the coordinator passes the findings into its prompt — it does not hand the subagent a new tool to go and fetch them.

13.3.label: Worth one look
13.3.text: A shorter anchor is more likely to be non-unique, not less. When Edit cannot find a unique match, Read then Write is the sanctioned fallback — not sed.
